successors.name: Greek city-states (independent poleis)
successors.text: Sparta, which kept its independence after Areus's death at Corinth (265)

ledger.x: 267 (or autumn 268): 'the anti-Macedonian faction under Chremonides' took power in Athens and 'declared war' on Antigonus Gonatas, allied with Areus I of Sparta and Ptolemy II.
267-261: rule 6 blend over Attica and the Isthmus, where Areus tried to break through to Athens.
262/261: Athens 'starved into surrender in either 262 BC or 261 BC'.
261: the war 'confirmed Antigonid control over Greece'; Athens 'lost her last pre-Hellenistic vestiges of political independence'.

wars.name: Chremonidean War
wars.outcome: 'Macedonian victory': Athens surrendered (262/261), Areus I killed (265), the Ptolemaic fleet beaten at Cos; 'Antigonid control over Greece' confirmed.

certainty.note: Two city-states and a fleet: the hatch covers their home territories, not a frontier.
